section.title: The ooSQLExtensions Class
section.para: The ooSQLExtensions class manages the extensions written in native code, typically C or C++, that ooSQLite can use besides the SQL functions and collations written in Rexx. It is not instantiated: all its methods and attributes are class methods and class attributes, as in .ooSQLExtensions~listBuiltins.

There are three kinds of extensions. The builtin extensions come from the SQLite source tree and are compiled into the ooSQLite library; they are registered on a connection with registerBuiltin, or on every new connection with autoBuiltin. An ooSQLite library is a shared library whose functions and collations are registered one by one, with handles: see loadLibrary. An ooSQLite package is a shared library that describes its own contents, so that it can be registered as a whole, on a connection or on every new connection: see loadPackage.

Libraries and packages are loaded once, and the class keeps them, so that getLibrary and getPackage can return them later. Plain SQLite extensions, which are not written for ooSQLite, are loaded with the oosqlLoadExtension routine.

section.title: lastErrCode (Class attribute)
section.para: Reflects the result code of the last method of the ooSQLExtensions class that was invoked.

listitem.para: A SQLite Result Code, or an ooSQLite specific result code. It is 0, OK, if the last method succeeded.
The Rexx programmer can not set the value of this attribute. It is set internally by the ooSQLite framework.

Every method of the class, except listBuiltins, sets the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes. They are always updated together: the message is always the one that goes with the code. Some errors, described in the documentation of each method, raise a syntax error instead, and then the attributes may keep the values of a previous method.

Besides MISUSE, the methods use these ooSQLite specific result codes: OO_PACKAGE_NOT_VALID when the package needs a newer version of ooSQLite or SQLite, OO_NO_SUCH_PACKAGE when the package is not loaded, OO_NO_SUCH_LIBRARY when the library is not loaded, and OO_PACKAGE_NOT_AUTOMATIC, OO_COLLATION_NOT_AUTOMATIC, and OO_FUNCTION_NOT_AUTOMATIC when what is stopped from being automatic was not. Loading a library that can not be found, or that lacks a function, gives the code of the operating system.

This example asks for a package that has not been loaded:
package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('noSuchPackage') if package == .nil then do say 'Error code: ' .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrCode say 'Error message:' .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrMsg say .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrCode == .ooSQLite~OO_NO_SUCH_PACKAGE end /* Output: Error code: 1007 Error message: package noSuchPackage is not loaded 1 */

section.title: lastErrMsg (Class attribute)
section.para: Reflects the error message of the last method of the ooSQLExtensions class that was invoked.

listitem.para: A message that explains the lastErrCode attribute, or no error if the last method succeeded.
The Rexx programmer can not set the value of this attribute. It is set internally by the ooSQLite framework.
See the remarks of lastErrCode.
See the example of lastErrCode.

section.title: autoBuiltin (Class method)
section.para: Makes builtin extensions automatic: they are registered on every database connection opened afterwards.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
name [optional]
The name of a builtin extension, an Array of names, or the keyword ALL, with case not significant. If it is omitted, or ALL, all the builtin extensions are made automatic. The names are base64, csv, ieee754, nextChar, percentile, regExp, rot13, spellFix, toType, and wholeNumber; listBuiltins lists them with a description. The case of the letters is not significant.
Returns OK on success, or a Result Code if SQLite could not make an extension automatic. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong.

A builtin made automatic is registered by SQLite itself on every connection opened afterwards, in this process: also the connections opened with the classic oosqlOpen routine. Making automatic a builtin that already is does nothing. cancelAutoBuiltin stops one or more builtins from being automatic, and resetAutoBuiltin all of them. The builtin extensions come from the SQLite source tree, and are compiled into the ooSQLite library: they are always available, nothing has to be loaded.
Raises a syntax error, 88.900, if a name is not the name of a builtin extension, and if the Array is sparse. The names of an Array are processed in order, and the method stops at the first error.
The functionality of the autoBuiltin method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_auto_extension API. The classic oosqlAutoExtension routine does the same for a single builtin.

This example makes the toType extension automatic, uses it on a new connection, and stops it from being automatic:
say .ooSQLExtensions~autoBuiltin('toType') conn = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(':memory:') say conn~exec("SELECT tointeger('42') AS n;", .true)[1]['N'] conn~close say .ooSQLExtensions~cancelAutoBuiltin('toType') conn = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(':memory:') say conn~exec("SELECT tointeger('42') AS n;") say conn~errMsg conn~close /* Output: 0 42 0 1 no such function: tointeger */

section.title: &changed11;autoCollation (Class method)
section.para: Makes a collation of a loaded package automatic, or stops it from being automatic.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
packageName [required]
The name of a package loaded with loadPackage. This is the name that the package gives itself, not the name of its file: see getPackage. The case of the letters is significant.
collationName [required]
The name of the collation in the package. The case of the letters is significant.
enable [optional]
True to make it automatic, false to stop it from being automatic. The default is true.

Returns true on success, false on error. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong. The errors are: the package is not loaded (OO_NO_SUCH_PACKAGE), the package has no collation with that name (MISUSE), too many automatic collations (MISUSE), and, when enable is false, the collation is not automatic (OO_COLLATION_NOT_AUTOMATIC).

An automatic collation is registered with the name that it has in the package. What is automatic is registered on each ooSQLiteConnection object when it is opened, after that: the connections that are already open are not changed. The automatic packages are registered first, then the collations, the collation needed callback, and the functions; if one of them fails, the rest are not registered, and no error is reported. Connections opened with the classic oosqlOpen routine do not get them. Up to 10 packages, 10 collations, and 10 functions can be automatic at the same time. Making automatic again something that already is does nothing.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, making automatic again something that already was added it a second time, so that it was still automatic after it had been stopped once.

This example makes the reverse collation of the examplePackage package automatic, and uses it on a new connection:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') say .ooSQLExtensions~autoCollation('examplePackage', 'reverse') conn = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(':memory:') sql = "WITH t(x) AS (VALUES ('a'), ('c'), ('b'))" - "SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x COLLATE reverse;" rows = conn~exec(sql, .true) do row over rows say row['X'] end conn~close /* Output: 1 c b a */

section.title: &changed11;autoCollationNeeded (Class method)
section.para: Makes the collation needed callback of a loaded package automatic, or stops it from being automatic.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
packageName [required]
The name of a package loaded with loadPackage. This is the name that the package gives itself, not the name of its file: see getPackage. The case of the letters is significant.
enable [optional]
True to make it automatic, false to stop it from being automatic. The default is true.

Returns true on success, false on error. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong. The errors are: the package is not loaded (OO_NO_SUCH_PACKAGE), and the package has no collation needed callback (MISUSE).

A connection can have only one collation needed callback, so only one can be automatic: making the callback of a package automatic replaces the one that was automatic before, from any package. Likewise, enable false stops the automatic callback, whichever package it came from. See the collationNeeded method of the ooSQLiteConnection class for what the callback does. What is automatic is registered on each ooSQLiteConnection object when it is opened, after that: the connections that are already open are not changed. The automatic packages are registered first, then the collations, the collation needed callback, and the functions; if one of them fails, the rest are not registered, and no error is reported. Connections opened with the classic oosqlOpen routine do not get them. Up to 10 packages, 10 collations, and 10 functions can be automatic at the same time. Making automatic again something that already is does nothing.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, a package without a collation needed callback made the method return false, but the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes said that there was no error.

The testPackage package, which is built with the examples, has a collation needed callback that registers the collations of the package when SQLite asks for them. This example makes it automatic, and then tries the examplePackage package, which has none:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('testpackage') say .ooSQLExtensions~autoCollationNeeded('testPackage') conn = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(':memory:') sql = "WITH t(x) AS (VALUES ('a'), ('c'), ('b'))" - "SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x COLLATE reverseOrder;" rows = conn~exec(sql, .true) do row over rows say row['X'] end conn~close .ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') say .ooSQLExtensions~autoCollationNeeded('examplePackage') say .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrMsg /* Output: 1 c b a 0 this package (examplePackage) contains no collation needed callback */

section.title: &changed11;autoFunction (Class method)
section.para: Makes a function of a loaded package automatic, or stops it from being automatic.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
packageName [required]
The name of a package loaded with loadPackage. This is the name that the package gives itself, not the name of its file: see getPackage. The case of the letters is significant.
functionName [required]
The name of the function in the package. The case of the letters is significant.
enable [optional]
True to make it automatic, false to stop it from being automatic. The default is true.

Returns true on success, false on error. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong. The errors are: the package is not loaded (OO_NO_SUCH_PACKAGE), the package has no function with that name (MISUSE), too many automatic functions (MISUSE), and, when enable is false, the function is not automatic (OO_FUNCTION_NOT_AUTOMATIC).

An automatic function is registered with the name and the number of arguments that it has in the package. What is automatic is registered on each ooSQLiteConnection object when it is opened, after that: the connections that are already open are not changed. The automatic packages are registered first, then the collations, the collation needed callback, and the functions; if one of them fails, the rest are not registered, and no error is reported. Connections opened with the classic oosqlOpen routine do not get them. Up to 10 packages, 10 collations, and 10 functions can be automatic at the same time. Making automatic again something that already is does nothing.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, making automatic again something that already was added it a second time, so that it was still automatic after it had been stopped once.

This example makes the half function of the examplePackage package automatic. The other function of the package, strAggregate, is not registered on the new connection:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') say .ooSQLExtensions~autoFunction('examplePackage', 'half') conn = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(':memory:') say conn~exec("SELECT half(5) AS h;", .true)[1]['H'] say conn~exec("SELECT strAggregate('x') AS s;") say conn~errMsg conn~close /* Output: 1 2.5 1 no such function: strAggregate */

section.title: &changed11;autoPackage (Class method)
section.para: Makes a loaded package automatic, or stops it from being automatic. All that the package contains is registered on every database connection opened afterwards.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
packageName [required]
The name of a package loaded with loadPackage. This is the name that the package gives itself, not the name of its file: see getPackage. The case of the letters is significant.
enable [optional]
True to make it automatic, false to stop it from being automatic. The default is true.

Returns true on success, false on error. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong. The errors are: the package is not loaded (OO_NO_SUCH_PACKAGE), too many automatic packages (MISUSE), and, when enable is false, the package is not automatic (OO_PACKAGE_NOT_AUTOMATIC).

An automatic package is registered as register does: its collation needed callback, its collations, and its functions, with the names they have in the package. A package can also be made automatic when it is loaded, with the makeAuto argument of loadPackage. What is automatic is registered on each ooSQLiteConnection object when it is opened, after that: the connections that are already open are not changed. The automatic packages are registered first, then the collations, the collation needed callback, and the functions; if one of them fails, the rest are not registered, and no error is reported. Connections opened with the classic oosqlOpen routine do not get them. Up to 10 packages, 10 collations, and 10 functions can be automatic at the same time. Making automatic again something that already is does nothing.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, making automatic again something that already was added it a second time, so that it was still automatic after it had been stopped once.

This example makes the examplePackage package automatic, and then stops it from being automatic:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') say .ooSQLExtensions~autoPackage('examplePackage') conn = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(':memory:') say conn~exec("SELECT half(5) AS h;", .true)[1]['H'] conn~close say .ooSQLExtensions~autoPackage('examplePackage', .false) conn = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(':memory:') say conn~exec("SELECT half(5) AS h;") say conn~errMsg conn~close /* Output: 1 2.5 1 1 no such function: half */

section.title: &changed11;cancelAutoBuiltin (Class method)
section.para: Stops builtin extensions from being automatic.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
name [optional]
The name of a builtin extension, an Array of names, or the keyword ALL, with case not significant. If it is omitted, or ALL, no builtin extension is automatic any more. The names are base64, csv, ieee754, nextChar, percentile, regExp, rot13, spellFix, toType, and wholeNumber; listBuiltins lists them with a description. The case of the letters is not significant.
Returns OK on success. A name, or a name of an Array, that is not automatic gives MISUSE; with ALL the result is always OK. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong.
Connections that are already open keep the extensions that were registered on them. resetAutoBuiltin also stops all the builtins from being automatic.
Raises a syntax error, 88.900, if a name is not the name of a builtin extension, and if the Array is sparse. The names of an Array are processed in order, and the method stops at the first error.
The functionality of the cancelAutoBuiltin method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension API. The classic oosqlCancelAutoExtension routine does the same for a single builtin.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, ALL, or no argument, returned MISUSE when some builtin was not automatic, which was nearly always the case, with a wrong message.
See the example of autoBuiltin.

section.title: getLibrary (Class method)
section.para: Returns a library loaded with loadLibrary.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
libraryName [required]
The base name of the library: the name of its file without the path, the extension, and, on Unix, the lib prefix. For example, the library loaded from user.extensions/libexamplelibrary.so is examplelibrary.
An ooSQLLibrary object, or .nil if no library with that name is loaded: then the lastErrCode attribute is OO_NO_SUCH_LIBRARY.
The ooSQLLibrary object gives the handles of the functions of the library, which the createFunction and createCollation methods of the ooSQLiteConnection class accept.
See the example of loadLibrary.

section.title: getPackage (Class method)
section.para: Returns a package loaded with loadPackage.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
packageName [required]
The name that the package gives itself, in its package entry, with the case of its letters. This is not the name of the file: the package examplePackage is loaded from the library examplepackage.
An ooSQLPackage object, or .nil if no package with that name is loaded: then the lastErrCode attribute is OO_NO_SUCH_PACKAGE.
The package object gives access to each collation and function of the package, and to its collation needed callback, so that they can be registered one by one: see the ooSQLPackage class.

The examplePackage package is in the examplepackage library:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('examplePackage') say package package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('examplepackage') say package say .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrMsg /* Output: an ooSQLPackage The NIL object package examplepackage is not loaded */

section.title: listBuiltins (Class method)
section.para: Lists the builtin extensions.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
print [optional]
If true, the list is also printed on the console, as a table. The default is false.

A result set with a record for each builtin extension, with two fields: NAME and DESCRIPTION. The format of the result set is the one set by the recordFormat attribute of the ooSQLite class, since there is no connection: by default, an Array of Directory objects. In the Array of Arrays format, the first item holds the names of the fields.
The builtin extensions come from the SQLite source tree, and are compiled into the ooSQLite library: they are always available, nothing has to be loaded. ooSQLite 1.1 has ten builtin extensions.
The names are the ones that registerBuiltin, autoBuiltin, and cancelAutoBuiltin accept, and the classic ooSQLiteRegisterBuiltin routine.

This example shows the start of each description:
do builtin over .ooSQLExtensions~listBuiltins say builtin['NAME']~left(12) builtin['DESCRIPTION']~left(50) end /* Output: base64 Implements a base64() SQL function to convert betw csv Implements a virtual table for reading CSV files. ieee754 Implements SQL functions for IEEE 754 binary64 flo nextChar Implements the next_char(A, T, F, W, C) SQL functi percentile Implements the percentile(Y, P) SQL function. regExp Implements a POSIX extended regular expression mat rot13 Implements a rot13() SQL function and a rot13 coll spellFix Implements the spellfix1 virtual table that can se toType Implements tointeger() and toreal() SQL functions. wholeNumber Implements the wholenumber virtual table that retu */

section.title: loadLibrary (Class method)
section.para: Loads an ooSQLite library: a shared library that contains collations and functions written in C or C++.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
libName [required]
The name of the shared library, or its path name. Without path information, the library is searched for as the operating system does: on Unix, the name is written as it is customary there, examplelibrary for libexamplelibrary.so, and on Windows the extension can be left out, so the same name works on both. With path information, the library is loaded exactly as specified: on Unix the name of the file must then be complete, as in libexamplelibrary.so; on Windows .dll can still be left out.
procedures [optional]
The name of a function of the library, or an Array of names, to resolve now. If it is omitted, each function is resolved when its handle is first asked for. The names of an Array are resolved in order; if one fails, the method stops there, returns false, and the names resolved before stay usable.
Returns true on success, false on error. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong. The library stays loaded when a function fails to resolve.

An ooSQLite library must export the ooSQLiteSetApi function, which the OOSQLITE_SET_API macro of the ooSQLite headers defines: a library that does not, such as a plain SQLite extension, can not be loaded, and the error message names the missing function. A plain SQLite extension is loaded with the oosqlLoadExtension routine instead.

Loading a library does not register anything. Its functions and collations are registered with the createFunction and createCollation methods of the ooSQLiteConnection class, with the handles that the ooSQLLibrary object gives, and under the names chosen there. The ooSQLite examples include the source of the exampleLibrary library.
Raises a syntax error if the Array of procedures is sparse; the library is then not kept.
The library is kept under its base name, which getLibrary uses. Loading a library with the same base name again replaces it.

This example loads the exampleLibrary library, and registers one of its functions and one of its collations:
names = .array~of('halfFunc', 'reverse') if \ .ooSQLExtensions~loadLibrary('examplelibrary', names) then do say 'Failed to load the library:' .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrMsg return end lib = .ooSQLExtensions~getLibrary('examplelibrary') say db~createFunction('half', lib~getHandle('halfFunc'), 1) say db~createCollation('reverse', lib~getHandle('reverse')) sql = "SELECT name, half(price) AS h FROM foods WHERE price IS NOT NULL" - "ORDER BY name COLLATE reverse;" rows = db~exec(sql, .true) do row over rows say row['NAME']~left(15) row['H'] end /* Output: 0 0 Bagels, raisin 0.75 Bagels 0.625 Bacon 1.875 */

section.title: &changed11;loadPackage (Class method)
section.para: Loads an ooSQLite package: a shared library that describes the collations and functions that it contains, and optionally registers it.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
libName [required]
The name of the shared library, or its path name, as for loadLibrary.
dbConn [optional]
An open ooSQLiteConnection object. If it is given, the package is registered on it, as register does.
makeAuto [optional]
If true, the package is also made automatic, as autoPackage does. The default is false.

Returns true on success, false on error. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong. A package that needs a newer version of ooSQLite or SQLite gives OO_PACKAGE_NOT_VALID, with a message that names both versions. A failure to register the package on dbConn is not reported: the method still returns true.

An ooSQLite package must export the ooSQLiteGetPackage function, which the OOSQLITE_GET_PACKAGE macro of the ooSQLite headers defines. The function returns the package entry, which gives the name of the package, the versions of ooSQLite and SQLite that it needs, and its collation needed callback, collations, and functions, each with its name. A package that needs a newer version of ooSQLite or SQLite is not loaded.

A package is registered as a whole on a connection with dbConn, with register, or with autoPackage; its parts are registered one by one with the methods of the ooSQLPackage class, autoCollation, autoFunction, and autoCollationNeeded. The ooSQLite examples include the source of the examplePackage package.

Raises an execution error, 98.900, if the connection is closed, and a syntax error, 88.900, if the argument is not an ooSQLiteConnection object. The connection is checked before the library is loaded.
The package is kept under the name that it gives itself, which getPackage uses. Loading a package with the same name again replaces it.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, a package that needed a newer version was refused, but the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes said that there was no error.

This example loads the examplePackage package and registers it on an open connection, which can then use its half and strAggregate functions and its reverse collation. The examplepackage library must be where the operating system looks for libraries:
if \ .ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage', db) then do say 'Failed to load the package:' .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrMsg return end sql = "SELECT name, half(price) AS h FROM foods WHERE price IS NOT NULL" - "ORDER BY name COLLATE reverse;" rows = db~exec(sql, .true) do row over rows say row['NAME']~left(15) row['H'] end sql = "SELECT strAggregate(name) AS s FROM foods WHERE type_id = 1;" say db~exec(sql, .true)[1]['S'] /* Output: Bagels, raisin 0.75 Bagels 0.625 Bacon 1.875 Bagels, Bagels, raisin */

section.title: registerBuiltin (Class method)
section.para: Registers builtin extensions on a database connection.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
dbConn [required]
An open ooSQLiteConnection object.
name [optional]
The name of a builtin extension, an Array of names, or the keyword ALL, with case not significant. If it is omitted, or ALL, all the builtin extensions are registered. The names are base64, csv, ieee754, nextChar, percentile, regExp, rot13, spellFix, toType, and wholeNumber; listBuiltins lists them with a description. The case of the letters is not significant.

Returns OK on success. A name that is not the name of a builtin extension gives MISUSE; an extension that fails to initialize gives the Result Code that it returns. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong.

Registering an extension again on the same connection does nothing more. The builtin extensions come from the SQLite source tree, and are compiled into the ooSQLite library: they are always available, nothing has to be loaded. Unlike autoBuiltin, which raises a syntax error for an unknown name, this method returns MISUSE.

Raises an execution error, 98.900, if the connection is closed, and a syntax error, 88.900, if the argument is not an ooSQLiteConnection object. Raises a syntax error, 88.900, if the Array is sparse. The names of an Array are processed in order, and the method stops at the first error.
The classic ooSQLiteRegisterBuiltin routine does the same for a single builtin.

This example registers two builtins on an open connection, and uses them; then it tries a name that does not exist:
say .ooSQLExtensions~registerBuiltin(db, .array~of('rot13', 'regExp')) sql = "SELECT rot13(name) AS r FROM foods WHERE name REGEXP '^Ba';" rows = db~exec(sql, .true) do row over rows say row['R'] end say .ooSQLExtensions~registerBuiltin(db, 'rot47') say .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrMsg~right(13) /* Output: 0 Ontryf Ontryf, envfva Onpba 21 found "rot47" */

section.title: resetAutoBuiltin (Class method)
section.para: Stops all the builtin extensions from being automatic.

listitem.para: There are no arguments.
Returns OK.

Since this is done by SQLite, it also cancels the extensions made automatic with the classic oosqlAutoExtension routine. The automatic packages, collations, and functions are not affected. Connections that are already open keep the extensions that were registered on them.
The functionality of the resetAutoBuiltin method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_reset_auto_extension API. The classic oosqlResetAutoExtension routine does the same.
See the example of autoBuiltin.
